about: INTERNAL: the order of the sales call script, read from two podcast episode transcripts (auto-generated, so paraphrased, not quoted). Members never see the source, its author or the acronym: they see the plain step names in "name". Ids can keep internal words; titles, outputs and files cannot.
rules: Run the six steps in this order.
Every step is led by questions, not statements, so the buyer does the talking.
Overview past pain until they have nothing left to add, then recap it back to them.
Sell the destination, not the flight: talk about the result they get, not the process. Keep the pitch short and break it into about three points.
Normal people have concerns. Expect them, and practice the answers until they are automatic, flashcards included.
The sale is not finished at the yes. Buyers judge you on the first 24 hours after they pay, so make specific promises for that window and keep them early.

steps.name: Why they're here
steps.goal: Get them to say, in their own words, why they took this call and why now.
steps.fromSource: Ask what made them get on the call, what their goal is, why it matters, and what it would look like if the ideal outcome happened.

steps.name: Name the problem
steps.goal: Say their problem back in one sentence and get a yes.
steps.fromSource: Summarize what you heard (what I'm hearing is you've done X and Y, and the missing piece has been Z) and confirm it is right.

steps.name: What they've tried
steps.goal: Learn what they already tried, why it didn't work, and what it has cost them.
steps.fromSource: Ask what they've tried before and why it didn't work. Keep going until there is nothing left, then recap the pain.

steps.name: Where they want to be
steps.goal: Paint the result in about three short points, then say the price and stop talking.
steps.fromSource: Sell the destination, not the flight. About three short points or stories tied to their problem.

steps.name: Clear the worries
steps.goal: Find the real concern and answer it with a question back.
steps.fromSource: Concerns fall into a few groups: the offer itself, time, money, the decision maker, and fear of making a mistake. Walk them through the decision: do you like what you heard, do you think it will get you the result, then what is your main concern.

steps.name: Lock in the yes
steps.goal: Right after the yes, make them glad they said it, and keep every promise for the next 24 hours.
steps.fromSource: After the sale, send something that makes the buyer feel good about it, like a personal video or a handwritten card. Buyers judge the business on the first 24 hours after purchase.
